summary.title: Software documentation guide
summary.one_liner: A community-maintained guide from Write the Docs covering best practices for writing software documentation, from getting started to docs-as-code, style guides, Markdown and API docs.
takeaways: Docs can be written and published with the same tools as code: issue trackers, version control, plain text, code review and automated tests (docs as code).
Good documentation is skimmable, exemplary, consistent, current and discoverable.
Style guides help keep voice, tone and terminology consistent across docs.
Markdown is the plain text syntax most docs tools accept, covering lists, headers and code.
The guide also covers building a documentation culture within a company and writing API documentation.
summary.summary: This is the Write the Docs community's software documentation guide, a living resource on best practices for software documentation and technical writing. It started as a way for developers to understand documentation and has since broadened in scope. The page is an index of topics: getting started, approaches, markup languages, tools, API documentation, and contributing. The listed highlights summarize key ideas such as docs as code, documentation principles, style guides, and Markdown, with the full content on linked subpages.
